name: Frances Brady
life: “I still remember a meter ticking through my younger child's first words.” On Saturday, near the window at Night Shift Donuts, Frances knows when the going-home crowd and the coming-to-work crowd will both be there.
voice: I sold my shares for a taxi license. I still own the pen that signed them away.
appearance: Frances is easy to recognize by iron-gray waves and a long face and high cheekbones. Usually dressed in a plum-colored cardigan with a pair of reading glasses in a cloth sleeve, Frances raises one eyebrow long before saying yes when listening.
personality: Frances never tires of being shown how somebody makes a living. Frances can ask an expert question of a craftsperson and still mishandle a simple emotional cue from a friend.
agenda: To get the old pen into a founding photograph.
family: Marlowe Arrieta is Frances’s second cousin. Frances remembers the birthdays. Marlowe asks what the birthday guest would like this year. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *A doctor moves away*, Marlowe says, “I asked for a last appointment to talk about anything other than my illness.”
connections: Grey Garza. The seller's old pen helps date the cassette of the founding meeting.

reactions.situation: An unexpected dividend arrives in the wrong envelope
reactions.response: Frances checks the payee's name with the teller before opening the envelope.

reactions.situation: Somebody says a missing friend must be avoiding their calls
reactions.response: Frances offers to accompany the caller to a familiar public meeting place without turning speculation into neighborhood news.

reactions.response: Frances may initially offer a repair, but sits down as soon as the request becomes clear.
